samples.summary: `stdoutSpy` is captured in the end-to-end suite but never asserted, so nothing checks the error body stays off stdout
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:109 creates `stdoutSpy = vi.spyOn(console, 'log')` purely to swallow output; no test in the file references `stdoutSpy` in an assertion. The whole point of the envelope contract is that errors go to stderr (see `outputError` doc comment, packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:49-56), yet a regression that also echoed the body on stdout (or emitted partial content before failing) would pass every test here. An `expect(stdoutSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` in the six-command loop would make the coverage real rather than incidental.
searchedFor: grepped the test file for stdoutSpy assertions

samples.summary: Two envelope-discrimination edge cases the new guard handles are untested: `{ error: null }` and the client's synthetic SESSION_EXPIRED envelope
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:80-84) has three conjuncts: typeof object, non-null, string `code`. The tests exercise the string case (EXPRESS_404), the missing/non-string `code` cases, and non-object bodies, but never `{ error: null }` — the exact input the `err !== null` conjunct exists for — so that conjunct could be deleted (typeof null === 'object', then `(null).code` throws a TypeError rather than returning false) without any test turning red. Likewise `HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody()` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:156-164) manufactures `{error:{code:'SESSION_EXPIRED',...}}` with `ok:false, status:401`; that is a real body reaching `forwardUpstreamError` and no test covers it.

samples.summary: The new command-level suite drives only failing responses; no test drives an `ok` response through the same six commands, so an inverted `!res.ok` guard would go unnoticed at the command level
samples.evidence: Every case in the CASES loop (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:157-180) stubs a 404 or a 409. The diff rewrote the guard at six call sites (docs.ts:197,249; notes.ts:148,195; slides.ts:154,197) into `if (!res.ok) return forwardUpstreamError(res)`. I grepped packages/cli/test for `parseAsync`/`registerDocsCommand`/`registerNotesCommand`/`registerSlidesCommand`: only namespaces, output, schema, tabs and this new file drive commander, and docs-content.test.ts / notes-content.test.ts / slides-content.test.ts exercise the `runXContent` modules directly, not the command action. So no test at any level asserts the success branch of these six actions still renders content after the refactor.
